header: Date: 2025-09-11 14:00 PDT | Duration: 57m | Recording: https://redwood-recordings/ff/ff-20250911-bc-00642 | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood), Ethan Liu (BlueCrest), Sofia Ramirez (BlueCrest), Liam O'Connor (BlueCrest), Hana Kim (BlueCrest)
summary: Kickoff technical onboarding for joint solution listing and certification. Reviewed marketplace requirements, deployment packaging options (AMI vs container + helm), networking/VPC peering constraints, security checklist (SOC2/KMS), and an initial benchmarking plan. Agreed on artifact handoffs and timeline for first compatibility run.
topics: Marketplace listing artifacts and tile assets
Reference architecture: container + helm vs AMI
Private deployment and VPC peering details
Automation: helm chart, terraform module, CI tests
Marketing/GT M coordination and co-sell signals
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right hello everyone, thanks for joining, we can go ahead and kick off. Um, quick roll call—this is Maya from Redwood, Jonas and Priya are here from our side as well.
[00:12] Ethan Liu: Hey thanks Maya, Ethan Liu here, Head of Cloud Partnerships at BlueCrest. Sofia, Liam, Hana with me.
[00:18] Sofia Ramirez: Hi everyone.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Morning all.
[00:23] Maya Patel: Great. The goal today is to align on the technical steps for getting BlueCrest's joint solution listed in the marketplace and to cover the reference architecture for both hosted and private deployment patterns. We'll also surface any security blockers. Jonas, want to lead the packaging discussion?
[00:38] Jonas Reed: Yeah sure. So high-level packaging choices we've seen are two main paths: an AMI / image-based offering for customers who want a single-click deploy, or a containerized helm chart for customers that want Kubernetes-native installs. Both have tradeoffs.
[00:52] Sofia Ramirez: Quick clarification: BlueCrest's customers are primarily k8s, they use EKS and GKE mostly, a small percent want marketplace AMI for air-gapped installs.
[01:03] Jonas Reed: Right, that helps — so helm chart should be first class. We'll provide a helm chart plus a small operator or init job to wire the KV cache, redis layer, and any model artifacts. Caveat: packaging the model weights — we need to confirm whether you want weights in an S3 bundle or to pull from Redwood private registry at runtime.
[01:22] Ethan Liu: We prefer S3 bundle with checksum verification. Some of our larger customers won't allow outbound pull to public registries.
[01:31] Priya Singh: Noted. We'll include both options in the docs but default to S3 bundle for marketplace.
[01:36] Hana Kim: On security — SOC 2 is table stakes. We also need to validate key management: can Redwood support customer-managed KMS for private deployments?
[01:45] Jonas Reed: Yes, we can support customer KMS via our private deployment connectors; for hosted we'd do envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys unless you sign an enterprise contract and enable BYOK. Sometimes our transcription accidentally says B-Y-O-K as 'by oak', hah, apologies.
[01:59] Liam O'Connor: (laughs) noted. For the marketplace tile we need a 1200x627 image, short description, one pager, and a listing JSON with deployment hints. Can you share the template?
[02:11] Maya Patel: Absolutely. I'll send the marketplace template and a sample listing JSON. We'll also attach an example tile asset and copy guidance.
[02:18] Jonas Reed: Back to networking — for private deployment we need VPC peering or transit gateway, and an option for AWS PrivateLink if customers want fully private endpoints. BlueCrest, do your customers prefer peering or PrivateLink?
[02:31] Ethan Liu: Peering is common, but PrivateLink is growing. We need the reference arch to show both. Also note some customers require specific CIDR ranges and egress restrictions.
[02:40] Sofia Ramirez: Can Redwood support per-tenant VPC peering or is it a shared infra model?
[02:44] Jonas Reed: We can do both. Dedicated has per-tenant VPCs; our dedicated offering supports isolated GPU pools. For the marketplace listing, we'll document the supported topology matrix: hosted API, dedicated/reserved, private VPC.
[02:58] Hana Kim: Regarding audit logs — we need to ensure all API calls, model pulls, and admin actions are retained for 90 days and accessible via our SIEM. Is that possible?
[03:08] Priya Singh: Yes, we expose audit logs to a customer S3 or syslog endpoint. We also have a push to Splunk/Datadog with a small adapter.
[03:16] Ethan Liu: Good. On performance: we'd like an initial benchmark run showing p50/p95 latencies at 1k concurrent users for your recommended config. What does Redwood need from us to run that?
[03:28] Jonas Reed: We'll need a representative prompt set, an input size distribution, concurrency profile, and a target sequence length. Ideally a small dataset — maybe 500 requests — to warm the cache then run the steady-state test. Also tell us the model variant you plan to ship.
[03:43] Ethan Liu: We'll share a 600-request set and indicate avg token length around 180 tokens. Model will be open-model-1-largish — still iterating.
[03:51] Maya Patel: Great. We'll provision a test cluster and run the compatibility benchmark. Jonas will own that.
[03:57] Jonas Reed: Yep. Test cluster will be container-based. For accurate cost numbers we may run quantized variant versus full fp16 so you can see tradeoffs. There may be some kernel noise depending on GPU type.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: About certification — the marketplace requires a security questionnaire and a verification call. How long does Redwood typically take to complete that?
[04:18] Maya Patel: Usually 1–2 weeks to fill initial questionnaire, then a 30–45 minute review call. If the vendor passes, marketplace ops does a 48-hour verification.
[04:27] Sofia Ramirez: Would the marketplace listing be co-branded? We want BlueCrest to appear as an official partner tile with Redwood listed as the runtime.
[04:35] Maya Patel: Yes, co-branded. We'll show both logos and link to joint docs. There are guidelines for logo usage which I'll include.
[04:42] Hana Kim: One blocker — data residency. Some of our EU customers require that model inference and logs remain in EU. Can Redwood pin the region for dedicated deployments?
[04:51] Jonas Reed: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API might be multi-region but we can designate EU-only for certain accounts with an enterprise agreement.
[05:00] Ethan Liu: OK perfect. One more thing: testing automation. Can Redwood provide a CI job or GitHub Actions sample to run smoke tests after deployment of your helm chart?
[05:09] Priya Singh: We have a GitHub Actions template and a small test harness to run healthchecks and a simple inference test. We'll attach that to the repo we share.
[05:18] Maya Patel: Great. I want to capture a few risks: packaging complexity (weights + S3), network edge cases for PrivateLink, and timeline slippage if SOC2 answers take longer. Anyone else?
[05:29] Liam O'Connor: Also image size — marketplace has an artifact size limit for AMI and container registry pulls may be slow for big weights. We may need a delta download approach.
[05:38] Jonas Reed: Good call — we'll propose a chunked download or manifest/partial fetch to speed installs.
[05:43] Sofia Ramirez: And dependency pinning — some customers will want exact libc/cuda versions.
[05:48] Jonas Reed: We'll include an environment matrix doc with recommended OS, docker, CUDA, and kernel notes.
[05:55] Hana Kim: For compliance we'll need to review your pen test schedule and any prior third-party audit reports.
[06:02] Maya Patel: I will push our security packet — SOC2 summary, pen test report redacted, and contact for compliance.
[06:09] Ethan Liu: Thanks. Timeline — if we get templates and assets quickly, we can aim for a soft listing by mid-October. Is that realistic?
[06:18] Maya Patel: Yes, soft listing mid-October is plausible. It depends on benchmark results and SOC2 sign-off.
[06:24] Priya Singh: To be concrete: Maya will send templates by 9/15, BlueCrest shares workload by 9/18, Jonas runs first benchmark by 9/26, and infra review week of 9/22.
[06:36] Jonas Reed: I'll log the benchmark run steps in the repo and include instructions for interpreting p50/p95. Please note the transcription may garble 'KV cache' as 'kay vee cache' in the notes, so we sometimes add parentheses.
[06:49] Lily? (mumble): [unintelligible]
[06:52] Maya Patel: Sorry, who was that?
[06:54] Sofia Ramirez: Probably Liam's kid in the background, all good.
[06:58] Ethan Liu: (laughing) yes, typical.
[07:02] Maya Patel: Any final questions?
[07:05] Hana Kim: Quick ask — does Redwood support bringing your own GPU AMI for private deployments? Some customers have vetted AMIs.
[07:12] Jonas Reed: We can support BYO AMI as long as it conforms to our node agent spec and we can validate the runtime. We'll add that to the compatibility doc.
[07:20] Maya Patel: Okay wrapping up: I'll send the marketplace checklist, tile spec, and security packet. Jonas will prepare helm/helm chart + test harness. BlueCrest will share dataset and infra contacts. We will reconvene after benchmark results.
[07:33] Ethan Liu: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:36] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[07:38] [call ends]
